title: Who entered the comparison?
hook: A toy company sample starts with winners. What changes when the omitted firms return?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Identify the omitted denominator before treating winner-only evidence as a general success rate.

misconception: A rule found only among selected past winners already explains success in the full population.
objective: Identify the omitted denominator before treating winner-only evidence as a general success rate.

claims.text: Original stipulated selection model: A inputs [10, 100, 0, 0] yield 100; B inputs [10, 100, 90, 0] yield 10. Prediction correct option 10. A reports {A}%; B reports {B}%. Adding 90 omitted non-winners changes the denominator from 10 to 100 without changing any firm’s result. These are invented groups; neither a causal explanation nor a replication of the book is supplied.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy showcase has 8 successful firms. The omitted 32 firms were unsuccessful. Success percentage in all 40? The numerator stays 8; the denominator is 40, so the full toy rate is 20%.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, selection, inputs [8, 100, 32, 0], output 20; independent Python recomputation.
